scope: Finite exact information ceilings for active acquisition and social-model identifiability. These results close the remaining bounded F2 theorem rows at G2; they do not establish a G6 morphology-to-capability predictor.
assumptions: all hypothesis/model classes, observation channels, query outcome alphabets and resource budgets are frozen before protected outcomes
information-acquisition queries are deterministic and noiseless at the registered interface, each query has at most A outcomes, and no target information arrives through an unmetered side channel
the active-acquisition counting theorem is necessary for any query family; tightness additionally requires a rich query family capable of realizing a separating A-ary code
social-model claims use a finite hidden-model set and a complete registered observation transcript before the held-out social query
social identifiability is zero-error and deterministic at this theorem scope; stochastic behavior, approximate Bayesian recovery and misspecified agent models require separate statistical treatment
evidence_class: P1 formal theorem family plus P2 exhaustive finite witnesses
strongest_parents: decision-tree / twenty-questions transcript counting and source coding
the already-registered deterministic observation-quotient ceiling plus statistical identifiability / inverse-planning theory-of-mind models
falsifier: A registered in-scope finite instance exceeds the transcript/identifiability ceiling while every information channel and theorem assumption remains exactly satisfied.

ceilings.quantity: K latent hypotheses, at most A outcomes per active query, at most q queries (or total budget B with uniform per-query cost c).
ceilings.theorem: Any deterministic adaptive q-query protocol with at most A outcomes per query has at most A^q complete transcripts, so zero-error identification of K latent hypotheses requires K <= A^q. Under uniform positive query cost c and total budget B, q <= floor(B/c), hence K <= A^floor(B/c). The count is tight when the registered query family can realize a separating A-ary code over the hypotheses.
ceilings.bound: K <= A^q; equivalently q >= ceil(log_A K) for A>1. With uniform cost: K <= A^floor(B/c).
ceilings.strongest_parent: Decision-tree leaf counting / twenty questions / finite source coding.
assumptions: deterministic noiseless active queries with at most A outcomes each
at most q acquired answers, or uniform positive query cost c under total budget B
no free side information, passive observation or intervention outcome carrying additional target information
zero-error identification; tightness only when the query family can implement a separating code
ceilings.negative_twin: Five hypotheses with two binary queries expose at most four transcripts, so exact identification is impossible; three binary queries are sufficient in a rich separating-query family.
ceilings.falsifier: An in-scope deterministic q-query protocol identifies K>A^q hypotheses with zero error, or a B-budget protocol with uniform cost c identifies more than A^floor(B/c) hypotheses without another information channel.

ceilings.quantity: Finite hidden agent-model set Theta, registered social observation transcript tau(theta), and held-out required social response g(theta).
ceilings.theorem: Given only the registered deterministic transcript tau(theta), a zero-error social-response decoder exists iff g is constant on every transcript fiber tau^{-1}(t). Full hidden-model identification is possible iff tau is injective. Therefore two goal/belief models that are observationally equivalent under all registered social observations but require different held-out responses are not identifiable without an additional discriminating observation or assumption.
ceilings.bound: The held-out response partition cannot refine the transcript partition; full identifiable model classes <= number of distinct registered transcripts.
ceilings.strongest_parent: The F2 deterministic observation-quotient theorem (direct social-domain corollary), statistical identifiability, and inverse-planning/Bayesian theory-of-mind models that infer hidden goals/beliefs from observed actions.
assumptions: complete deterministic social transcript available before the held-out response is frozen
no direct hidden-state label, private-state access or unregistered diagnostic interaction
required held-out social response g is fixed prospectively
ceilings.negative_twin: Two hidden models produce the same observed action in the base context but require different held-out predictions; no transcript-only decoder can answer both. A registered diagnostic probe that makes their transcripts differ restores identifiability.
ceilings.falsifier: A transcript-only decoder gives different correct responses to two models in the same transcript fiber, or fully identifies two hidden models with identical complete registered transcripts.
